title: Game runtime status
description: B1, status up: what a game runtime reports to the control plane's status listener. World truth comes from the plugin's count of the loaded world's objects, not from container health.

generation.description: The generation the runtime is running.

state.description: installing: downloading SteamCMD or the server, or waiting to retry a download that failed. loading: launched, the world not yet reported. running: the world loaded. unverified: launched, but the plugin has not reported a world that had nothing to lose: no save, or last seen empty. held: restoring a backup before the game starts; before the install, for a world with no save whose newest restore did not end done, so no new world is made in its place, until another restore is asked for; or stopped before its first autosave because the world loaded empty, or the plugin never reported it, although it held objects when last seen or, with nothing remembered, a save existed. The container stays up, except after a restored save that loaded empty is swapped back, when it starts again.

reason.description: Why the runtime is held or unverified, or why its install is being retried, in one line of printable text: vhd status shows it to the server manager.

objects.description: The loaded world's object count, as the plugin last reported it. Absent while the plugin's report is missing or stale.

players.description: Players connected, as the plugin last reported it. Absent while the plugin's report is missing or stale.

backups.description: The world's backups, as the runtime last listed its backup folder. Absent until the runtime has listed its backup folder, or failed to.

names.description: The backups in the folder, newest first, each named for when it was taken, in UTC, so the first says the newest one's age. At most 200, which the manifest's backups.keep and keep_daily, 100 each, keep a folder within; until the next backup prunes it, as after either is lowered, only the newest 200 are named.

failure.description: Why the runtime could not take or keep its backups, in one line of printable text: vhd status shows it to the server manager. Absent once a turn of its backups succeeds.

restore.description: The newest restore the runtime has acted on, as its generation named it. Absent until it acts on one.

id.description: The restore's id, as the generation gave it.

outcome.description: restoring: replacing the save, or world truth has not judged the restored save yet. done: the world loaded the restored save: world truth passed it, or it held no objects and the plugin never reported it. failed: the restore was refused, and the world's save was left as it was. rolled-back: the restored save loaded empty or ended the game as it loaded, or a newer generation dropped or replaced the restore before world truth judged it, and the save it replaced is back.

reason.description: Why the restore failed or was rolled back, what it waits on, or that the save it replaces could not be backed up and is only kept aside, in one line of printable text: vhd status shows it to the server manager.
